title.narrative: PK Punjab Irrig Agri Productivity Improvement Program Project

description.narrative: The objective of the Punjab Irrigated Agriculture Productivity Improvement Program Project for Pakistan is to improve productivity of water use in irrigated agriculture. This will be achieved through improved physical delivery efficiency and irrigation practices, crop diversification and effective application of inputs which will translate into greater agricultural output per unit of water used. There are four components to the project, the first component being installation of high efficiency irrigation systems. This component will include construction of high efficiency irrigation systems such as drip, bubbler, sprinkler, over an area of about 120,000 acres. It will also support provision of precision land leveling equipment for improving land leveling operations in the country and thus improving irrigation application efficiency. This will result in higher productivity of water. The second component is the improvement of community irrigation systems. This component will cover improvement of watercourses in canal irrigated areas, as well as in the rain fed areas. The watercourse level water users' associations would be established and they would receive support to improve about 9,000 watercourses. The third component is the improved agriculture technology or practices and monitoring and evaluation. This component will support improvement in irrigation agronomy, demonstration of and assistance in improved and modern technologies and methods to increase agriculture production. Finally, the fourth component is the project management, supervision, technical assistance, training and strategic studies. This component will support the Government of Punjab's efforts in project management, construction supervision, checking delivery of works, quality and certification of payments, strategic studies, technical assistance and training to staff, etc.

The project?s main objective is to improve productivity of water use in irrigated agriculture. This will be achieved through improved physical delivery efficiency and irrigation practices, crop diversification and effective application of inputs that will translate into greater agricultural output per unit of water used. The project?s objectives would contribute to increased agricultural production, employment and incomes, higher living standards and positive environmental outcomes.

comment.narrative:
<p>It should be noted that no definition of improved agricultural practices was provided in the original results framework presented in the PAD. The Project M&E Consultants interpreted that improved agricultural practices include adoption of HEIS, PLL and other modern technologies. Since installation of HEIS and PLL has been introduced throughout all the project area (covering 36 districts of Punjab), it is considered as fully achieved.</p>
<p>However, there is some data available on access to trainings that indicateintroduction of improved agricultural practices. Some 6.1% of watercourse beneficiaries report receiving any training including trainings from agriculture extension, OFWM, and private sector. Compared to this, 35% of HEIS beneficiaries responded that they received training through farmers days and 55% of them reported them as being useful. By these estimates, all 9,577 HEIS beneficiaries(100%) and about 20,000 non-HEIS farmers on watercourses (6.1% of 321 thousand) received training on improved agricultural practices.</p>

title.narrative: Improvement of watercourses in canal command

comment.narrative:
<p><em>Achievement ratio; 192% of original and 150% of revised targets</em> ???????</p>
<p>Original target was set as 9000 watercourses to be improved in canal command areas, however, at additional financing of the project, not only the target was enhanced but also the measuring indicators were defined in three sub-components. All the targets set by sub-components were achieved as 112%, 202% and 169% respectively</p>

<p>At the time of appraisal the project aimed to give 3,000 laser land levelers. However because of the success of the activity at the time of restructuring the target was increased to 5,000. The target has been achieved (100%).</p>

<p>At the time of project appraisal this indicator was measuring number of HEIS units (target for year 6 was 17,520), however at the time of additional finance the indicator was changed to measure area under HEIS with a target of 120,000 acres land . The achievement of this is at 90,000 acres (75%) and 9577 units (55%) at completion </p>

title.narrative: Reduction in water losses in the project area

target.value: 45% level of current losses reduced in 11,550 W/C improved by 10% and 120,000 acres of HEIS

comment.narrative:
<p>At the time of appraisal the indicator was set based on coverage of watercourses and HEIS. However, the M&E has gathered more outcome level indicator of reduction of water losses in watercourses and HEIS.</p>

<p>The original target of 10% improvement in water losses was substantially achieved even at the time of additional financing. Therefore, the unit of measurement was revised and target fixed as 45% reduction of water losses at 11,550 watercourses. Average results of a study reveals that water delivered as 62.32 LPS at head of unimproved watercourse reached as 24.05 LPS at tail, which shows losses about 61%; whereas water delivered as 64.40 LPS at head of improved watercourse reached as 16.45 LPS at tail showing water losses as 25.6%. It implies the reduction in losses amounts to 57% (against target of 45% reduction) at 17,300 watercourses against target of 11,500 watercourses (achieved 126% of the original target for water savings and about 150% of target of number of watercourses), thus the targets have been achieved substantally. Achievement ratio; 126%</p>

<p>At additional financing, target of 120,000 acres covered by HEIS was fixed, against which 90,000 acres were covered by HEIS at completion. <em>Achievement ratio; 75%.</em>???????</p>

<p>A 47% reduction in use of fertilizer was also achieved through HEIS.</p>

actual.value: 57% of current losses reduced by improving 17,300 watercourses and setting up HEIS on 90,000 acres

title.narrative: Increased agriculture output per unit of water used (watercourse)

comment.narrative:
<p>The baseline refers to the value of produce using conventional ways (watercourses) and estimated at 7 Rupees per m3 for Row Crops (wheat, maize, cotton, sugarcane etc.) and targeted (45% increase) at 13 Rupees per m3 of water. The targets assumed an efficient use of water in timely manners. No change was proposed at additional financing.</p>
<p>At completion, estimation of water productivity was estimated using constant 2012 prices. Average value of water productivity is estimated at Rs 16/m3 against target of Rs 13/m3 (i.e. 120% increase).</p>

title.narrative: Technologies demostrated in the project areas

comment.narrative: <p>This indicator was introduced at additional financing. The target of HEIS technology installation was achieved as 75%. Installation of HEIS technology was spread throughout the project area, at 9577 sites, and covered all the 36 districts.</p>

title.narrative: Percentage of women members in WUAs that are project beneficiaries

comment.narrative:
<p>While the indicator asks for percentage of WUA members who are female the target asks for number of WUA with a female member. Because these are different measures the end result is represented in both ways.</p>
<p>If we disaggregate this number before and after restructuring (when this indicator was added to the results framework), we see that in the WUA set up after restructuring, 21% ofmembers were female and 52% of WUA had at least one female member (compared to 5% and 12% respectively before restructuring). So the project did make significant efforts to ensure women participation after the indicator was added to the RF but could not restructure the WUA already set up to include more women. The zero baseline reflects pre-project situation.</p>

actual.value: 16.5% of WUA have at least one female member while 7% of WUA members are female

title.narrative: Increased agriculture output per unit of water used (HEIS)

comment.narrative:
<p>The baseline refers to; value of produce using HEIS (for vegetables, orchards etc.) and estimated as 12 Rupees per m3 of water and targeted (45% increase) as 17.40 Rupees per m3 of water; The targets assumed an efficient use of water in timely manners. No change was proposed at additional financing.</p>
<p>At completion, estimation of water productivity was estimated using constant 2012 prices; thus the average value of water productivity has been computed as Rs 35/m3 against target of Rs 17.40/m3 (i.e.200% increase)</p>

title.narrative: Clients who have adopted an improved agr. technology promoted by the project (number of households)

comment.narrative: <p>This indicator was introduced at additional financing. The indicator did not set target for counting the number of clients who adopted an improved agr. Technology promoted the project, but mentioned the area under HEIS technology, which was 75% achieved. Besides, the data shows that 9577 farmers adopted this technology including at 5746 orchard farms; 1341 vegetable farms; 1149 field crops; and 1341 row crops.</p>

title.narrative: C3 (b) Percentage of agro-processing and value-addition facilities that employ women

comment.narrative: <p>This subcomponent was not implemented and no results were achieved.</p>

title.narrative: Number of women employed on HEIS units per acre

comment.narrative: <p>This indicator was added at the time of additional finance. Against the target of at least 3 women employed HEIS units per acre,the project achieved an average of 5 women employed on HEIS units per acre. The women generally employed at HEIS farms for field works, for example picking, handling and bagging of fruits and vegetables; picking of cotton; etc.</p>

title.narrative: Percentage of beneficiaries that feel project investments reflected their needs and brought improvements (disaggregated by gender)

comment.narrative: <p>This indicator was introduced at additional financing. In response to a question to beneficiary farmers about their perception if there was any improvement due to project interventions, 98% farmers responded in affirmation. This question was put to 1644 farmers during face to face farmers including 1355 farmers at watercourses; 194 HEIS owners; and 115 farmers who availed project support for irrigation schemes. </p>

title.narrative: C3 (a) Processing units (equipment and facilities) for value-added production

comment.narrative: <p>This subcomponent was not implemented and no results were achieved.</p>
